name: Lamar Jackson
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Lamar did Lamar things... Ran wild, dropped dimes, and made defenses dizzy. Still one the most dangerous dual threats in the game.

name: Baker Mayfield
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Baker found redemption in Tampa. Career-high yardage, 41 TDs, and has been running more. Now can he do it again?

name: Kyler Murray
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Kyler’s still got the wheels—and when he uses them, defenders panic. If the Cards unleash him, you’re getting 10+ rush TD upside.

name: Ja'Marr Chase
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a walking highlight reel whose fantasy production is as explosive as his on-field personality. Draft him and enjoy the show. He led the NFL in receptions (127), receiving yards (1,708), and receiving touchdowns (17) in 2024

name: Patrick Mahomes II
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Still the best QB on Earth. Patrick may not have won fantasy leagues last year, but he’s a postseason assassin with great weapons returning. The calm before the storm?

name: Brock Purdy
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Purdy’s combined 51 passing touchdowns over the past two seasons ranks eighth among all quarterbacks (just behind Patrick Mahomes’s 53), and the wily signal caller also offers some sneaky (deceptive, even) rushing value as a bonus. Purdy is a savvy scrambler (61 scrambles in the past two years, 10th most) who can pick up first downs with his legs and extend plays when they break down. He averaged over four fantasy points per game last year just from rushing—and that type of fantasy boost gives him top-10 potential again in 2025.

name: Jayden Daniels
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Jayden went from NCAA highlight reel to NFL cheat code. Led all rookies in fantasy and runs like he owes defenders money.

name: Jalen Hurts
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Jalen's got the most unstoppable play in football and a nose for the end zone. Tush push? More like auto TDs.

name: Joe Burrow
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Joe looked elite when healthy, averaging 22.5 PPG. If he’s back to full strength, he’s a top-5 lock with top-3 upside.

name: Josh Allen
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Josh didn’t just play—he ruled. Josh puts up MVP stats, runs like a RB, and slings like a sniper. Fantasy gold every week.

name: Caleb Williams
NFLPlayerCardInfo: There wasn’t a whole lot that went well for Williams during his rookie year, but he did at least flash the fantasy upside that many thought he’d have. Williams notched five top-six weeks, including an overall QB1 performance in Week 6. If Williams can play within his offense more and cut down on sacks in year two under the tutelage of Ben Johnson, he’ll produce a whole lot more spike weeks for your fantasy squad.

name: Justin Fields
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Fields had the second-most rushing yards for a QB ever in 2022 (1,143) and is now the Jets’ starting QB. New York is likely to double down on the run after ranking dead last in rush attempts last year. From Week 5 on in 2022, Fields was behind only Josh Allen, Jalen Hurts, and Patrick Mahomes in points per game.

name: Justin Jefferson
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The only thing more beautiful than his route running is his contract extension. He's the WR1 with the highest floor in fantasy football. He had 103 catches for 1,533 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2024

name: Bo Nix
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The Broncos added TE Evan Engram, RB J.K. Dobbins, and drafted RB RJ Harvey and WR Pat Bryant to help Bo Nix follow up his stellar rookie year, which saw him finish as the QB8 in fantasy. Nix looks to be a fantastic fit with Sean Payton, and will use his sneaky rushing ability (430 yards, four TDs) behind one of the league's best offensive lines to provide a high floor in fantasy this season. For the first time since high school, Nix is playing under the same head coach, play caller, and quarterbacks coach for a second straight offseason.

name: Dak Prescott
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Prescott led the NFL in passing touchdowns (36) in 2023 while completing nearly 70 percent of his passes, showing he’s still capable of operating a scorching-hot Dallas offense. In addition to CeeDee Lamb, Prescott now has receiver George Pickens to throw to. That’s the best no. 2 wideout for Dallas in years.

name: Justin Herbert
NFLPlayerCardInfo: After overcoming some early-season injuries, from Weeks 7 to 18 Herbert ranked fourth in passing yards per game, ninth in rushing yards per game, and 10th in fantasy points per game at the QB position. This offseason the Chargers added some rookie talent in RB Omarion Hampton and pass catchers Tre Harris and Oronde Gadsden II. Herbert is still on an offense that wants to run the football, but his talent as a thrower and runner keeps him in the mix as a QB1.

name: Jared Goff
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Goff is capable of putting up big-time numbers in the passing game, but he’s a zero as a runner. Still he's on one of the best offenses, but we'll see how he does without his offensive coordinator.

name: CeeDee Lamb
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's Dak Prescott’s best friend and the Cowboys' entire offense. His volume is a cheat code, and he's a lock for triple-digit receptions. He finished 2024 with 101 catches for 1,194 yards and six touchdowns

name: Saquon Barkley
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The Madden Cover star led the NFL in touches in 2024 and held up remarkably. With over 2,000 rushinge yards, Saquon reminded us he’s still elite. Volume and efficiency like that is rare, but can he do it again?

name: Puka Nacua
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The league is still trying to figure out if he's actually human. His rookie season was a fluke, and his sophomore season was even better. He’s the real deal.

name: Derrick Henry
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The King isn't dead yet, he just moved his kingdom to Baltimore. He's a bulldozer, not a dance partner. Last year at age 30, he rushed for over 1,900 yards

name: C.J. Stroud
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Stroud was spectacular as a rookie, finishing as the QB8 in fantasy points per game by throwing 23 touchdown passes and just five picks while adding three rushing scores. Despite his disappointing sophomore slump in 2024 (he dropped to QB28 in points per game), a top-10 finish remains in Stroud’s range of outcomes. He needs to cut down on sacks and create more big plays, but he still has the talent to bounce back closer to his rookie performance.

name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The Sun God is a PPR monster. He gets targets, he gets yards, and he gets touchdowns. He's a safe bet for a top-5 WR finish.

name: Bijan Robinson
NFLPlayerCardInfo: From Week 6 on, he was the RB1 in fantasy. With an actual QB under center, Bijan’s gonna feast. This is the breakout season you were promised.

name: Brian Thomas Jr.
NFLPlayerCardInfo: One of the most explosive deep threats in the league, but he'll need to prove he's not a one-trick pony. He'll have some massive weeks and some duds, but his ceiling is worth the risk.

name: Josh Jacobs
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The RB 1 on the Green Bay Packers has led the league in touches, with little competition this year, he could do that again.

name: Nico Collins
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's the clear-cut WR1 in a high-octane offense. The volume is there, the talent is there, and now the stats are too. He had 68 catches for 1,006 yards and seven touchdowns in just 12 games in 2024

name: Davante Adams
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's still a superstar, even on a new team with a crowded receiver room. He'll get his targets, and he’ll make plays. His value is higher than his ADP but him and Stafford need to stay healthy.

name: Jahmyr Gibbs
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He’s electric, explosive, and faaast. Draft him and watch him score in bunchesas he led all running backs with 16 rushing touchdowns in 2024

name: Malik Nabers
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A second year player who might just lead the league in targets this year. He's dynamic and shifty when he gets the ball and can score on any play

name: Drake Maye
NFLPlayerCardInfo: One of the last QBs you’ll find in a fantasy draft who is definitely a starter and can run. Maye demonstrated outlandish talent last season but is getting a major upgrade in his coaching staff as well as in the talent around him.

name: Tee Higgins
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The number two in Cincinnati is a surefire fantasy WR2 with WR1 upside. He finally got his contract, and with Ja'Marr Chase drawing all the attention, Higgins is primed for a huge season.

name: Tua Tagovailoa
NFLPlayerCardInfo: One of the league’s most productive pocket passers when healthy, but staying healthy is the hard part. While Tua’s health is his biggest concern, he played all 17 games in 2023 and led the NFL in passing yards.

name: De'Von Achane
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Achane's speed is a cheat code and his big-play ability is unmatched. Fun Fact: He averaged an outrageous 7.8 yards per carry as a rookie.

name: A.J. Brown
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a top 5 receiver in football, but he's on a team that runs the ball among the most in the league. He'll win you weeks and have week's where he's real quiet

name: Sam Darnold
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Sam Darnold led his team to 14 wins, but still will always be known for his memes

name: Trevor Lawrence
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Lawrence could see a dramatic improvement in 2025 thanks to the arrival of new Jags head coach Liam Coen and his quarterback-friendly scheme. It won’t hurt, either, that Lawrence has a new big-time playmaker in Travis Hunter. After seeing Coen help turn Baker Mayfield into the QB4 in fantasy last year, it’s hard to put a ceiling on what he could do with Lawrence in Jacksonville.

name: Jordan Love
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Love’s numbers in 2024 were stunted by injuries suffered throughout the season to his knee, shoulder, and elbow. When healthy, though, Love brings the upside to lead the league in passing touchdowns (he was second in 2023 with 32). He’s a big-play hunter with the arm strength and aggressiveness to make every throw and, critically, is surrounded by a talented core of young playmakers.

name: Matthew Stafford
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Stafford had a down year in the touchdown pass department in 2024, tossing just 20 scores, but it’s easy to see that number bouncing back closer to 30 this year, especially with the addition of red-zone monster Davante Adams. Stafford, who has averaged 28 passing touchdowns per 17 games over his 16 year career, could be a sneaky quarterback streamer this season or a solid QB2 in superflex.

name: Kyren Williams
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Kyren Williams scored 14 TDs and 1300 rushing yards last year. He's the go to when the Rams are in the red zone

name: Cam Ward
NFLPlayerCardInfo: #1 overall pick in last year's draft, but can he turn around the worst team in the league? He's got a good arm, and a playmaker, but time will tell

name: Christian McCaffrey
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The fantasy GOAT is still someone to consider even with the injury risks. He's the highest floor and highest ceiling in fantasy football. He is one of only two players to ever rush for 1,000 yards and have 1,000 yards receiving in a single season.

name: Ashton Jeanty
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A rookie with an elite college resume and first-round draft capital. Expect a monstrous workload from day one. He came within 27 yards of Barry Sanders’ single-season rushing record at Boise State in 2024.

name: Drake London
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Drake London is finally free from the constraints of Arthur Smith's coaching. He's a target monster with a new, more aggressive offense. He's a high-end WR2 with WR1 upside.

name: Ladd McConkey
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Last year Chargers rookie hit the ground running with an electric connection with Justin Herbert. He's a PPR machine and could be a league winner.

name: Geno Smith
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Smith was QB16 last year in points per game and is now being drafted outside of the top 20 at his position. Even if the Raiders take a more run-balanced approach to their offense, Geno stands to benefit from a better offensive line, great weapons, and a competitive division that should produce plenty of high-scoring games.

name: Michael Penix Jr.
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Atlanta’s new golden boy is a high-risk, high-reward pick with a rocket arm, but an injury history. In his three starts in 2024, he led all rookie quarterbacks with a 87.6 Pro Football Focus passing grade.

name: Bryce Young
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Young revitalized his career in the middle of last season, returning from his benching to lead a league-average unit. With new receiver Tetairoa McMillan, Young could be a perfectly middle-of-the-road QB.

name: Tyreek Hill
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The Cheetah is still the most dangerous deep threat in the league. His production is a bit more volatile now, but his big-play ability is worth the risk.

name: J.J. McCarthy
NFLPlayerCardInfo: It’s not ideal that he missed his entire rookie season to a meniscus tear, but McCarthy should benefit greatly by playing in one of the most quarterback-friendly offenses in football. Kevin O’Connell is a wizard at scheming guys open, and McCarthy will be throwing to the likes of Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson. The second-year pro could be far more efficient than expected—and maybe even prolific—in his debut season.

name: Aaron Rodgers
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Rodgers' fantasy value is a wild ride, fueled by drama, conspiracy theories, and the ghosts of his Achilles tendon. Still he threw 28 TD passes and he's top 5 in the NFL all time in that category

name: Mike Evans
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a veteran who knows how to get open, even in a crowded receiver room. He's had 11 straight seasons with at least 1,000 receiving yards.

name: Terry McLaurin
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He finally got a new QB in Jaden Daniels, and put up great numbers last year. However this year he hasn't practiced with the team much as he hopes to get a new contract

name: Jonathan Taylor
NFLPlayerCardInfo: It's been a while since he was the overall RB 1, but Taylor still has the juice, and little competition in Indianapolis

name: Bucky Irving
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A rookie breakout star, Irving is primed for an even bigger role this year. He's a league-winning talent waiting to happen.

name: Breece Hall
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The talent is undeniable, but the Jets offense is still a question mark. A new offensive coordinator brings a new system, making his fantasy outlook a high-risk, high-reward play.

name: Xavier Worthy
NFLPlayerCardInfo: His speed is a cheat code. He's a big-play threat who could be a boom-or-bust fantasy option, but his connection with Patrick Mahomes is something to watch.

name: James Cook
NFLPlayerCardInfo: His fantasy value is touchdown-dependent and he's due for regression. The volume is there, but a crowded backfield and a dip in scores could spell trouble.

name: Rashee Rice
NFLPlayerCardInfo: His off-the-field issues are a concern, but his on-field production is not. He's an explosive receiver in a high-powered offense with Patrick Mahomes at the helm.

name: Anthony Richardson Sr.
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's the Happy Gilmore of QB's he can throw it a mile, but can't hit a player 5 yards away consistently.

name: Joe Mixon
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Mixon's value is tied to his health and his usage. There are too many storm clouds to warrant an early draft pick, but over the last four years, he has averaged 1,377 yards from scrimmage per season.

name: Alvin Kamara
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Approaching his age-30 season on a team in transition, Kamara's receiving work will keep his floor high. He might not get the same high-end volume, but he's still a PPR machine.

name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
NFLPlayerCardInfo: JSN is a PPR monster who is a threat to break out at any moment. With a new offensive coordinator, he should finally be unleashed.

name: Kenneth Walker III
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's ultra-efficient with the ball in his hands, but his long-term health is a concern. A new system and a potential committee could limit his upside, but his big-play ability is a game-changer.

name: DJ Moore
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a target magnet who is a safe bet for a high-end WR2 finish. He's a great route runner with a knack for making big plays, but he's still a risky play with inconsistent quarterback play

name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The generational prospect didn't exactly have a generational rookie year, but with a full season under his belt, it's a different story. He's a technician with Hall of Fame bloodlines. While he might have been a disappointment in fantasy last year, he did tie the Cardinals' rookie record for receiving touchdowns with eight.

name: Zay Flowers
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Lamar Jackson’s top target and the engine of the Ravens passing attack. He's a shifty route runner with game-breaking speed.

name: DK Metcalf
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He’s a physical freak. Even with a new team and QB, he’s a dominant fantasy player. He finished 2024 with 66 catches, 992 yards, and 5 TDs

name: Chase Brown
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He emerged as a workhorse in 2024 and is primed for an even bigger role. His versatility as a rusher and receiver makes him a high-floor, high-ceiling option. From Week 4 on in 2024, he was the RB6 in fantasy scoring.

name: James Conner
NFLPlayerCardInfo: His new deal and a clear role make him a valuable mid-round pick if you're willing to gamble on his health. He's only the third player in Cardinals history with multiple 1,000-yard rushing seasons.

name: Garrett Wilson
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He finally has a quality QB, and his fantasy production will soar. He's an elite route runner who will be a target monster.

name: David Montgomery
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The thunder to Jahmyr Gibbs' lightning, Montgomery is a touchdown machine, but he’s aging and could see a dip in volume. A new offensive coordinator might also shift the balance in the backfield.

name: Aaron Jones Sr.
NFLPlayerCardInfo: At 31 years old, the veteran is entering a committee backfield. He may still have some juice left, but his workload and efficiency are in question. He's finished as a top-15 fantasy RB in five of the last six seasons.

name: Calvin Ridley
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A volatile deep threat who is a boom-or-bust fantasy option on a new team. The Titans are a run-heavy team, but he'll still get his shots downfield.

name: George Pickens
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's an explosive deep threat who can win with his size and speed. His fantasy value is highly dependent on his new quarterback, but the ceiling is sky-high.

name: Chuba Hubbard
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Fresh off a breakout season and a new contract, Hubbard is a fantastic value. The Panthers' improving offense and his dual-threat ability make him a safe bet for weekly production.

name: D'Andre Swift
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Back with his old offensive coordinator, Ben Johnson, Swift is set for a fresh start. His usage in the passing game and his big-play ability make him a high-end RB2 with RB1 upside.

name: Jordan Addison
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A talented wide receiver who's now the clear-cut #2 option in the Vikings' passing attack. He’s a big-play threat with a knack for finding the end zone. He had 63 catches for 875 yards and 9 TDs in 2024

name: Courtland Sutton
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a touchdown machine and a red zone weapon, but his production is tied to inconsistent quarterback play

name: DeVonta Smith
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He’s a crisp route runner who is arguably the best WR2 in the league. He'll have spike weeks, but other weeks where he's phased out of the offense. He finished 2024 with 68 catches for 833 yards and 8 TDs.

name: Russell Wilson
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Try his signature sandwitch. It's called the Danger Witch and it's dangerously good. Be careful though. It's spicy.

name: Omarion Hampton
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The Chargers' first-round pick is a physical runner with a monster college production profile. He's primed to be the lead back in a run-heavy offense under Jim Harbaugh.

name: Tony Pollard
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The days of Pollard as a highly efficient back are over. He's now a touchdown-dependent runner in a committee. He’s best used as a flex option in fantasy, hoping for a spike week.

name: Jameson Williams
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Finally healthy, he's a true difference-maker. He’s a speedster who can take the top off a defense and he's poised for a breakout season. He finished 2024 with 58 catches for 1,001 yards and 7 TDs

name: Trey McBride
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He’s a target monster who is the focal point of his offense. He’s a high-volume TE with a massive target share. He finished 2024 with 111 catches for 1,146 yards.

name: George Kittle
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a human wrecking ball who plays with reckless abandon. The veteran TE is a consistent high-end fantasy option with an incredible knack for big plays.

name: Brock Bowers
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Last year Bowers broke every TE rookie record in the book. He's a tight end with a WR's skillset and a QB who needs a security blanket. His volume is a cheat code. He finished his rookie season with a whopping 112 receptions for 1,194 yards.

name: Jerry Jeudy
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Now with a new team and a QB who actually throws the ball, Jeudy is a prime breakout candidate. He's a crisp route runner who is poised for a career year. He had a career-high 90 catches for 1,229 yards in 2024.

name: Jakobi Meyers
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A reliable and consistent receiver who will provide a solid floor for your fantasy team. He won't give you massive spike weeks, but he's a great option in PPR leagues. He finished 2024 with 87 catches for 1,027 yards.

name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The versatile weapon has had some down years, but with a new team, he's a prime candidate for a bounce-back. His value is tied to his health and his usage, so be wary

name: Chris Godwin
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Godwin is a dependable receiver who provides a great floor, but his ceiling is limited by a crowded receiver room. He's a great WR3 in PPR leagues.

name: Travis Hunter
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A rookie with superstar potential on both sides of the ball. His fantasy value is directly tied to his usage, but he's a game-breaking talent who could be a league winner.

name: Rome Odunze
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The rookie wide receiver is a polished route runner with elite size and speed. He's an instant contributor in a new-look offense. He finished 2024 with 54 catches for 734 yards and 3 TDs.

name: Jaylen Waddle
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A big-play threat with a new QB who loves to push the ball downfield. He's a boom-or-bust fantasy option who could have some massive weeks.

name: Cooper Kupp
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The veteran receiver is a consistent PPR producer, but injuries and age are a concern. He's still a high-end WR2, but he's no longer the fantasy WR1 he once was.

name: Jauan Jennings
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The 49ers' slot receiver is a sneaky fantasy option who could be a league-winner. With Deebo Samuel gone and Brandon Aiyuk recovering from a torn ACL, Jennings is set up for a huge season.

name: Jayden Reed
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A dynamic weapon with the ability to turn a short catch into a massive gain. He's a player who makes his own luck. He finished his 2024 season with 55 catches for 857 yards and six touchdowns.

name: RJ Harvey
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A rookie second-round pick, Harvey is a lightning-fast and shifty runner in Sean Payton’s offense. While he may split carries with J.K. Dobbins, his receiving skills and explosiveness give him immense upside.

name: Keon Coleman
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The rookie's transition to the NFL was a little bumpy, but his physical tools are undeniable. He has a chance to be a red zone monster and the WR1 in Buffalo

name: Brian Robinson Jr.
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A healthy Robinson could be the Commanders' workhorse. He is an early-down thumper who can catch passes, giving him a great floor and a solid ceiling.

name: TreVeyon Henderson
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A dynamic back with elite speed, he landed in a great situation with the Patriots. He may not get a full three-down workload, but his big-play ability makes him a threat to score on any touch.

name: Kaleb Johnson
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The rookie out of Iowa product is a powerful downhill runner who projects as the early-down back in Pittsburgh's run-heavy offense.

name: Matthew Golden
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A talented rookie who will fight for a role in a crowded receiver room. He has a great combination of speed and strength, but his opportunity is a concern.

name: Khalil Shakir
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a great receiver but on the smaller side and plays in 3 reciever sets. He had 76 catches for 821 yards and four touchdowns in 2024.

name: Quinshon Judkins
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Might not play much this season because of an off the field court case

name: Tetairoa McMillan
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A big-bodied rookie wide receiver with a massive catch radius and a knack for making contested catches. He was a top 10 pick in the NFL Draft

name: Chris Olave
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A talented wide receiver who's in a run-heavy offense and has to deal with a new QB. His fantasy value is a bit of a mystery as he's a great reciever on a bad offense and has health issues of his own.

name: Ricky Pearsall
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a perfect fit for a Shanahan-style offense. Pearsall got shot his rook year and still finished the season with 65 catches for 965 yards and four touchdowns.

name: Tyler Shough
NFLPlayerCardInfo: This rookie was the 40th overall pick in a bad QB class and will be fighting for a spot

name: Darnell Mooney
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He finished his 2024 season with 64 receptions for 992 yards and five touchdowns. Should be the WR 2 in Atlanta

name: Isiah Pacheco
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Pacheco is poised to be a workhorse back in one of the league's best offenses. His physical running style and nose for the end zone make him a high-end RB2. He led the Chiefs in rushing yards and touchdowns despite missing nine games in 2024

name: Rhamondre Stevenson
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A new offense and a new coach means a blank slate for Stevenson. He's a powerful runner with pass-catching upside, but his fumbling issues are a major concern.

name: Michael Pittman Jr.
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A target hog with a new contract. Pittman is a good not great reciever on a terrible offense

name: Tyrone Tracy Jr.
NFLPlayerCardInfo: One of the few brighter spots for the Giants last year, could be a lead rusher, but on a team that projects for one of the lowest points int he league

name: Javonte Williams
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Now with the Cowboys, Williams is looking to recapture his pre-injury form. He's once was a tackle-breaking machine  but he had a career-low 3.7 yards per carry in 2024

name: Sam LaPorta
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The sophomore slump hit hard, but he’s still a red zone threat in a high-powered offense. He’s a consistent TE1 with a high floor. He finished 2024 with 60 catches for 726 yards and seven touchdowns.

name: Stefon Diggs
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a proven veteran with a Hall of Fame resume, but injuries and age are a concern. He's a boom-or-bust fantasy option who could be a WR1 if he stays healthy. He finished his 2024 season with 47 receptions for 496 yards and three touchdowns before tearing his ACL.

name: Travis Kelce
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a future Hall of Famer, but father time is undefeated. His production has been on the decline, but he's still a top-tier fantasy TE because of his volume and connection with Mahomes

name: Rashid Shaheed
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A speed demon who can take the top off a defense and make big plays. He's a great bench stash who can give you a couple of explosive weeks.

name: Jaylen Warren
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A dynamic and explosive player, Warren is the lightning to Kaleb Johnson's thunder. He'll get plenty of touches as a receiver out of the backfield

name: Austin Ekeler
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The veteran running back is a high-floor PPR option in his new home in Washington. While he won't be a workhorse, his role as a pass-catching specialist will give him plenty of value.

name: Brandon Aiyuk
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A torn ACL in 2024 have dampened his fantasy value. He’s a risky pick, but the talent is there if he can get back on the field. He only played in seven games in 2024 and isn't expected to start the season

name: Quentin Johnston
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The Chargers rookie is a boom-or-bust fantasy option who needs to prove he can catch the ball consistently in the NFL

name: Cam Skattebo
NFLPlayerCardInfo: A rookie with a physical style and pass-catching chops make him a fascinating fantasy prospect. He rushed for 1,715 yards and 21 touchdowns in his final college season.

name: Mark Andrews
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a touchdown machine and a red zone weapon, but his volume is a concern. He's a great TE1, but he needs to stay healthy and fend off Isaiah Likely.

name: Wan'Dale Robinson
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a PPR machine who makes a lot of catches, but doesn't do much with them. Still a solid producer with 93 catches for 699 yards

name: Rashod Bateman
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Finally healthy, Bateman broke out as a red zone threat. He's a great value pick who could be a consistent WR2.

name: Adam Thielen
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The veteran receiver is a consistent PPR producer, but his age is a concern. He’s a great WR3 in PPR leagues, but don't expect many huge games.

name: David Njoku
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Njoku is tough as nails as he burned his face last year and still played football. He's a high-end TE1 with top-5 upside if he can stay healthy. Still the offense is a concern.

name: Zach Charbonnet
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Still in a committee with Kenneth Walker III, Charbonnet's role is a bit of a mystery. He's an efficient runner, but he needs a bigger workload to be a consistent fantasy producer.

name: Christian Kirk
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The veteran slot receiver is a reliable option for your fantasy team, but he's no longer the high-end WR2 he once was. His fantasy value is directly tied to his targets and a deep receiver room.

name: Rachaad White
NFLPlayerCardInfo: The former lead back now finds himself in a committee with rookie Bucky Irving. His pass-catching ability will keep him relevant, but he’s no longer a sure thing for a massive workload.

name: Najee Harris
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's got one eye - supposedly. Hard to see a clear path for a ton of playing time if news about his eye injury doesn't improve

name: Marquise Brown
NFLPlayerCardInfo: "Hollywood" Brown is a boom-or-bust deep threat with WR1 upside if he can stay healthy. He finished his 2024 season with a career-low nine receptions for 91 yards and no touchdowns in just two games.

name: Tyjae Spears
NFLPlayerCardInfo: Spears is a dynamic pass catcher, but hard to know how many touches he will get on an offense that has been one of the worst in the league

name: Josh Downs
NFLPlayerCardInfo: He's a dynamic slot receiver who can make big plays. He’s a great PPR option, but his value is tied to inconsistent quarterback play. He finished 2024 with 72 catches for 803 yards and five touchdowns.

name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
NFLPlayerCardInfo:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt’s nickname is “Bill”. He tells the story that as a kid, he had a shaved, bald head, so his friends called him “Little Bill” in reference to the cartoon character. 

“Bill” was a zero-star recruit from Montgomery, Alabama who played at Alabama State for 4 seasons, then New Mexico, and then Arizona. Which brings me to the whole reason he didn’t get an NFL Combine invite - he played just ONE game at Arizona in his final season of college football.
